_meta.note: The second history of shtetl, branch v2: foundations and houses (containers and systems alike) as actors in one C daemon over ZFS. A foundation is one dataset in zlake whose builds are snapshots, beamed to zrun; when a version reaches zrun each house on that foundation rolls onto it: stop, final save, replay into a new version named for the foundation snapshot, swap, start. A failed roll stalls that one object; copies converge to their owner's; old versions are pruned by count once the beam is consistent. The plan is implementation-plan.md beside this file, the author's words its section 18; open-questions.md holds what waits on the author. Paths are relative to the shtetl repository root. Drive this file with tools/tracker.py (its default file). STATE 2026-10-18: the fourteen questions ruled; M0's probes written, their box and VM runs owed; the issues of M1 to M7 are written at rulings-1.
_meta.first_history: branch main (4c0f2c7): its docs/planning.md rulings and probe results are evidence; its code is not carried except the configuration language (plan section 12)
_meta.terminology: house = a container or a system; version = one dataset of a house, cloned from one foundation version; active = the version a house runs from, its newest complete one and the only one mounted; roll = a foundation's next build, or a house's move onto the next version of its foundation; swap = the one act that makes a house's new version active; stall = a roll that failed, the object rolling no more until a person restarts it; shake = merge a recipe's layers into the shaken recipe, injected read-only into what it built; remote = a named place shtetl reaches, a git repository or the lake; beam = a dataset's copy converging to its owner's; owner = the space where a dataset is written.

milestones.M1: the skeleton: the C tree, its gate and make check; the ZFS layer with its fake; the daemon's loop, an actor that starts from ZFS after a crash, and the command over the socket
milestones.M2: shake: the language carried and trimmed, the remotes; a shaken recipe made and injected
milestones.M3: foundations: a real build in zlake on the box, a stall and a restart, pkg, the builder
milestones.M4: beam and prune: both directions, resume after a cut, the counts, pruning that waits for the beam
milestones.M5: containers: create, save, pkg, the roll on a foundation's arrival, the swap, a stall; a real jail rolled across two foundation versions on the box
milestones.M6: systems: outer space, boot environments, a roll through a reboot, on a VM
milestones.M7: status and syslog, the notifier's interface, the clock

probe-harness.description: The box harness for M0's probes, after main's probes/ (972314c) and tests/box/send.sh (90f58e7), written fresh: sudo sh probes/run.sh [P1 ...] runs the named probes (all by default) on throwaway pools over swap-backed memory disks, refuses to start if a pool of its names exists, and destroys only what it made. Every check prints ok or failed with its probe and cell; the log opens with the shtetl commit it ran at and ends with '== N ok, M failed'. The box commits the log under probes/results/<host>-<time>/ and pushes it (su to SUDO_USER, pull --rebase, push; SEND=no keeps it local). Verify: sh -n on the mac; on the box, run.sh with no probe prints the header and '== 0 ok, 0 failed', and leaves no pool or memory disk behind.
probe-harness.provides: Any probe runs on the box (or the VM) and its log comes back as a commit.
probe-harness.note: 2026-10-18 d0cd4e0: written, sh -n/dash -n clean, --list/usage/refusal checked on the mac; box run owed. Worklog issue-docs/probe-harness.md.

probe-resume.description: P1 (plan section 14): between two md pools standing for zrun and zlake, a full send, an incremental and a clone stream (a house version cloned from a foundation snapshot the lake already has), each received resumable (zfs receive -s, which shtetl will reach as lzc_receive_resumable), each cut part way by killing the sender, each resumed from receive_resume_token (zfs send -t), each ending with the source's guids. Also: a dataset holding a token refuses a fresh receive until it is resumed or aborted (-A), so 'resume if there is a token, else send' is the whole rule. Verify: the probe's cells green on the box.
probe-resume.provides: Evidence for section 8.1: a beam cut anywhere converges on the next attempt with nothing destroyed.
probe-resume.note: 2026-10-18 57e8ed7: P1.1-P1.10 written; box run owed. Worklog issue-docs/probe-resume.md.

probe-live-link.description: P2: a jail created with path=/containers/H where H is a symlink to v1 (a dataset mounted at /containers/v1, a minimal tree enough to run /bin/sh); the link switched to v2 with rename(2) while the jail runs; the jail stays on v1 (a file written inside lands in v1; jls -n path shows v1's path); jail -r, then jail -c, lands in v2; mount.devfs mounts under the resolved path and jail -r unmounts it; jexec works throughout. Verify: the probe's cells green on the box.
probe-live-link.provides: Evidence for section 7.4 and open question 6: a container's switch is one rename of a link.
probe-live-link.note: 2026-10-18 d6d8a22: P2.1-P2.7 written; P2.7 records devfs left when the link moves under a running jail. Box run owed. Worklog issue-docs/probe-live-link.md.

probe-house-data.description: P5: a house's own dataset v1/www with three saves; v2/www cloned from v1/www@final; v2/www promoted; v1 destroyed whole; v2/www holds v1/www's saves and its contents; a lake copy of v1/www converged before the promote and of v2/www after it, incrementally where ZFS allows and with whatever it needs where it does not (recorded either way). Verify: the probe's cells green on the box.
probe-house-data.provides: Evidence for sections 7.1 and 8.2: a house's own data moves to a new version by clone and promote, and the lake can follow.

probe-roll-live.description: P6: a house version with three saves of real edits (files added, changed, removed, and one edit that conflicts with the foundation's change and is answered); replayed onto a newer foundation version into a new dataset with zfs_rebase as plan 7.2 step 2 says, while the live version takes a fourth save; the fourth caught up as 7.3 step 3 says; the result compared, tree and attributes, with a replay of all four done at once while nothing ran. probe-boot-envs.description: P3, on a FreeBSD 15.1 VM with root on ZFS that the author provides: two system versions under a systems dataset of the boot pool, each with var and usr/local children, roots mountpoint=/ canmount=noauto; bootfs set to one, rebooted, then the other; each boots with its own children mounted (rc.d/zfsbe) and none of the other's; the loader's boot environment menu lists both and boots either by hand; bectl list shows them. Verify: the probe's cells green on the VM, its reboots driven by the probe across runs.
probe-boot-envs.provides: Evidence for section 7.4: a system's versions are boot environments and its switch is bootfs.
probe-boot-envs.note: 2026-10-18 3b62deb: P3.1-P3.7, four runs over three reboots, stage from ZFS; version children canmount=noauto (zfsbe before zfs mount -a). VM run owed. Worklog issue-docs/probe-boot-envs.md.

probe-outer-space.description: P4, on the P3 VM: the outer space protocol as ruled 2026-10-15 (a swap-backed memory disk made a pool, the current root sent into it, vfs.root.mountfrom set, reboot -r); an rc script in the sent root that, finding / on the memory pool, snapshots a dataset of the disk pool, sets bootfs to the other version and reboots for real; the machine comes up on the new bootfs. Records how long the send and the reroot take and how large the memory disk had to be. Verify: the probe's cells green on the VM.
probe-outer-space.provides: Evidence for section 7.4: a system stops into outer space, switches there, and comes back on the new version.
probe-outer-space.note: 2026-10-18 720760e: P4.1-P4.8, three runs; outer space reports through s2probe:* properties on the disk pool; stage 1 always starts over. VM run owed. Worklog issue-docs/probe-outer-space.md.

spike-port.description: S1 (plan section 14): an Elixir release built on FreeBSD 15.1 from lang/elixir, holding a supervisor and a gen_statem that rolls a toy foundation (write a file, snapshot, clone the snapshot, send it to a second md pool) through a C port: one process speaking the external term format over stdin and stdout with erl_interface's ei, calling libzfs_core (lzc_snapshot, lzc_clone, lzc_send, lzc_receive) and returning nvlist facts as terms, no text. The actor is killed at each step and started again, and finds where it stood from ZFS alone. Measured and written in spike/README.md: the release's size on disk, resident memory idle, start time, the port's round trip. Verify: the spike's cells green on the box. Its code stays in spike/ until the ruling decides its fate.
spike-port.provides: The numbers and the experience section 10's choice is made from.
spike-port.note: 2026-10-18 fccf203: port, release and probes/S1-runtime.sh written; zport.c compile-checked on the mac (mac OpenZFS headers, stub ei.h); the Elixir never compiled (no Erlang on the mac). Box run owed: pkg install elixir; sudo sh probes/run.sh S1. Worklog issue-docs/spike-port.md.

spike-outer-space.description: S2: the S1 release started by rc on P4's memory-disk root, finding its toy foundation's state on the disk pool and finishing a roll there before the real reboot. Measured: its start time on the memory disk. Verify: the cells green on the VM; the numbers in spike/README.md.
spike-outer-space.provides: Evidence that the chosen runtime can carry a system's switch through outer space.
